condition: # BoxLang Compatibility Transfer ## Goal Every BoxLang JVM test (`../BoxLang/src/test/...`) has a 1:1 black-box counterpart as a MatchBox `.bxs` script under `tests/scripts/boxlang_compat/`. The runner (`tests/boxlang_compat_tests.rs`) executes them all. This is **transfer-first**. Getting the equivalent behavior green is a separate follow-up task that uses only MatchBox/Rust idiomatic solutions — NOT a rewrite of VM internals to mirror the JVM. ## Mapping conventions - Directory structure mirrors `../BoxLang/src/test/java/ortus/boxlang/...`. - One `.bxs` per BoxLang test file. - Each JVM `@Test` method becomes a block using `assert <expr> : <TestName> `. - Add a comment or somehow mark the file so that we know which JVM test it ties back to. ## Categorizing Tests We only want to transfer tests that capture BoxLang runtime behavior. When you are evaluating a specific test to decided if you should transfer it you should consider the following. - Is it BoxLang source being evaluted directly? Transfer it verbatim. - Is it a unit test that focuses on Java behavior or internal BoxLang behavior? Skip it. The goal is not to reproduce the JVM implementation - only the BoxLang execution behavior. ## Status per category | Category | Files | Status | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | operators | AKgT | transferring | | types | — | pending | | scopes | — | pending | | casters/dynamic | — | pending | | bifs/* | — | pending | ## Skipped tests (hard requirements, non-JVM) Documented here as they are identified. A test is skipped only when it cannot be expressed in MatchBox (JVM-only infrastructure such as Java reflection, SOAP wire format, JDBC driver internals). Functionality that CAN be expressed (e.g. configuring a datasource + running queries) is transferred.
